positive_controls.argument: Identified operational failures, load patterns and completed corrective-action checks expose realized constraints that a trade study must address or can use to reject an infeasible alternative.
Configuration-linked operational evidence can reveal an envelope exceedance, unexpected degradation or missing case and thus trigger bounded reconsideration of qualification assumptions.
Systemic investigation and checked corrective actions supply evidence about causal scenarios and implemented control performance, enabling the hazard record to change with actual operation.
Observed behavior, anomaly diagnosis and evidence that corrective actions work provide current information about technical and operational deficits before a transition is expanded or repeated.

Relevant signals and configuration-linked incident analysis help choose a viable response and check whether the claimed restoration occurred rather than merely whether a recovery command returned success.
Owned incident learning and actual failure patterns inform maintenance, obsolescence response and whether a support intervention changed recurrence risk.

Operational observations and checked actions reveal consequence, detectability and failed-control assumptions, supporting a proportionate revision of the named control rather than automatic escalation by phase.
An incident reconstruction can separate diagnosis, edit, propagation, contractual unwind and recovery losses, showing which costs arise from concrete mechanisms rather than calendar lateness alone.
